title: Aggregate battery status across all packs
head: 56b8b4900a8e
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Charge-unit packs with both energy_now and charge_now are mixed with UPower's differently normalized energy-full
leads.consequence: UPower 1.91.4 chooses charge units based on charge_full (when energy_full is absent), computes energy and full at design voltage, and explicitly ignores an optional energy_now on such packs. The new script takes energy_now first but still divides by UPower energy-full. A charge-unit BAT0 with UPower energy 18Wh/full36Wh and sysfs energy_now 15Wh, alongside BAT1 at 20/40Wh, reports 46% instead of UPower DisplayDevice's 50%. The panel's UPower icon and script numbers disagree, and its time uses the wrong numerator. Use matching UPower energy or match UPower's unit selection for numerator and denominator.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1); corroborated; published within finding 1

leads.summary: Signed current_now can cancel another pack's rate and erase time/rate
leads.consequence: The kernel documents negative current_now for discharging and positive for charging, and UPower takes fabs for each pack. With one -1A/10V discharging and one +1A/10V charging, this loop adds -10W and +10W as 0W. It reports discharging, rate 0W and a blank remaining time although both packs carry current (UPower's sum of magnitudes is 20W). Normalize each rate before aggregation, and decide how to represent conflicting directions rather than allowing cancellation.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F6, pre-existing path); not published (unlikely on x86 ACPI)

leads.summary: A present but dead pack with nonzero historic energy-full is counted as active capacity
leads.consequence: A pack can remain present with zero live energy but positive energy-full (the case described by open #12789). Nothing checks liveness or present. A 0/20Wh dead BAT0 plus a 20/20Wh working BAT1 produces 50% and 4h to full here, rather than the live pack's 100%; consumers show the erroneous combined figures. UPower 1.91.4 DisplayDevice itself also counts a present dead pack, so replacing this with DisplayDevice alone does not solve this shape. Exclude dead packs using evidence beyond energy-full while retaining healthy zero-charge packs.
leads.triage: already in Opus related-PR context (#7916); DisplayDevice shares it; not published

leads.summary: If both packs lack full-energy telemetry, their known percentages are thrown away
leads.consequence: UPower still prints energy-full: 0 Wh for a battery lacking energy_full/charge_full, while a separate capacity percentage can be known. Its DisplayDevice averages percentages when total full energy is zero. With two packs at 40% and 60% and no energy telemetry, the script emits 0% instead of 50%. This is a silently hidden valid interface case and misleads the panel and plain notification. Fall back to available per-pack percentages when no usable full-energy data exist.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q3, M15, rare); not published

leads.summary: Cycle count zero means unknown, but the new combined list presents it as a measured cycle count
leads.consequence: Kernel power_supply ABI says cycle_count=0 means unavailable, and UPower maps it to unknown. BAT0 with 0 and BAT1 with 115 becomes cycles 0, 115, rendered verbatim in the power panel rather than distinguishing unknown from a real count. Skip or label invalid counts on each pack, do not represent zero as a measured cycle. Open #12484 fixes unavailable cycles on the single-pack path but would need to cover the new multi-pack loop.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F4); published as additional note; #12484 existence verified via gh api

leads.summary: A BAT-named device-scope peripheral can reverse the system battery state
leads.consequence: UPower -e enumerates all devices; its generic power_supply backend can report a type Battery, power supply: no device whose native BAT name matches grep. DisplayDevice explicitly excludes devices without power-supply. A real charging BAT1 listed first and a device-scope discharging BAT0 listed second used to report charging via the old first-pack path, but now produces discharging and a time to empty based on BAT1's stored energy. Filter type, present and power-supply before adding a pack; hardware shape is supported by upstream, not confirmed for any named peripheral.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (Q2) confirmed with real upower client; published in finding 3

leads.summary: The multi-pack path drops UPower thresholds, then reports the first BAT* sysfs threshold as if it applied to all packs
leads.consequence: battery_info is set only for pack_count==1, so the per-pack UPower charge-start/end fields are discarded for two packs; the fallback always reads the first BAT* directory, even if it is absent, phantom, or has a different limit from the selected pack. With BAT0 limit 80 and BAT1 limit 90, the aggregated status reports just threshold 80% and on AC may call the aggregate state holding according to that unrelated limit. Open #13292 adds a regression test requiring thresholds and cycles from real BAT1 when phantom BAT0 precedes it. In that fixture limits appear only in BAT1's UPower report (no sysfs threshold files), so this loop would omit threshold entirely and emit cycles 1, 80 instead of just 80; if phantom BAT0 also has sysfs threshold files, the fallback selects those instead. Establish a per-pack threshold policy and exclude non-present devices before showing one aggregate hold.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); published as finding 2; #13292 existence verified, not cited

leads.summary: A readable sysfs attribute whose read fails replaces UPower's good energy/rate with zero
leads.consequence: Kernel power_supply's show callback returns driver -ENODEV/-EAGAIN/-ENODATA errors even while the attribute exists and is readable. The code tests -r, then passes the unchecked $(<file) result to awk; a failed read becomes numeric zero rather than falling back to UPower. In a multi-pack refresh that zeros one pack's energy and/or rate, potentially falsely showing low percent/0W and blank time. The same existing single-pack rate bug is addressed in open #12755, but that PR's diff patches only the old single-pack rate path and would not guard this newly added loop; adapt its checks for each pack and both energy/rate.
leads.triage: behavioural; follow-up Q1 confirmed (bash probe, R06/R08/R10); published as additional note; #12755/#12649 verified open

leads.summary: The new multi-pack test cannot tell a live sysfs energy read from ignoring sysfs entirely
leads.consequence: Each fixture's sysfs energy_now equals the corresponding UPower energy value. A plausible broken implementation replacing the new sysfs energy branch with only UPower's energy still passes every assertion (mutant run exit 0). Add one pack whose UPower energy is stale and whose sysfs energy differs, then assert percentage/time based on the intended source; this would catch the mutant and expose the mixed-unit convention issue. This is a test-fidelity gap, not a claim that the existing aggregation negative control is weak: the kept test fails on base and current quattro.
leads.triage: dropped: moot under the suggested UPower-energy change

leads.summary: Concurrent #12445 independently replaces the same loop and test, with incompatible aggregation decisions
leads.consequence: Open #12445 (diverged, not stacked) also replaces the first-pack selection with an independent multi-pack loop and appends its own test. Its diff does not apply to this PR head: the script's loop hunk and the test's appended hunk both fail. It chooses charging over discharging and a per-pack minimum time, while this PR chooses discharging over charging and total-energy time; #12445's new fixture provides 20Wh + 30Wh, 6W + 4W, and asserts 2h; this PR's loop instead calculates 50/10 = 5h, so that fixture would fail against this branch. If both merge without reconciling the loop and test, the second change overwrites or conflicts with the first and at least one set of fixtures loses its intended behavior. Choose one policy and combine the tests before either merge.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #12445 open, same files, body says closes #11990, different policy; published in related PRs with 'computed, not run' qualifier

leads.summary: Case-sensitive BAT filter silently omits real system batteries with other names
leads.consequence: The new loop still sees only lines containing uppercase BAT. Snapdragon qcom-battmgr-bat has UPower name battery_qcom_battmgr_bat, so this script prints nothing despite a present system battery. The power panel has DisplayDevice present and keeps old/empty batteryInfo, while the notification sends an empty status. This is a pre-existing omission, but the claim to aggregate every present pack and the newly added silent no-pack exit do not cover this shipped device shape. Related open #13029 supplies a separate recognition fix; preserve its non-BAT system-battery handling while integrating aggregation.
leads.triage: pre-existing, verified #13029 open; not published (outside PR claim)

leads.summary: A vanished UPower object produces a success-shaped empty result and stale cached panel data
leads.consequence: UPower 1.91.4 upower -i reports an invalidated path as 'failed to set path: ...' but exits success, so the || continue guard does not detect it; the missing native-path does cause a skip. When the only listed pack vanishes between -e and -i, the command exits 0 with no stdout. While UPower's DisplayDevice still reports a present battery, the panel deliberately keeps its last nonempty batteryInfo, showing stale percentage/time for that refresh; if DisplayDevice updates to absent, the panel closes. The notification receives an empty status string. If skipping vanished packs is intended, emit a distinct failure/absence status or clear stale consumers instead of returning indistinguishable success.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F5); follow-up Q3 corrected premise with real client; published in finding 3

- Opus and the Sol hunter ran in parallel. Opus finished in about 19 minutes and Sol in about 25.
- 6 of Sol's 12 leads corroborated Opus.
- Sol's lead on the competing PR #12445 was new, and a direct `gh api` check confirmed it.

- The self-check caught two wrong table-row descriptions and a dozen lost qualifiers (voltage_min_design versus voltage_max_design, the energy_full absence condition, "tested" versus "every").

- The first editorial pass flagged a missing **Impact** on the third finding and a **Minor:** label. Future drafts should give every headed finding an Impact paragraph and use neutral labels such as "Additional notes" from the start.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** in the tested cases with `energy_*` packs, the aggregated figures match what UPower's DisplayDevice gives (the source the bar icon already uses). That covers the Surface Book 2 numbers in the new test, the ThinkPad T480 table in #6885 and the T480 on-AC table in #8864. Single-pack output is unchanged in all 12 single-pack shapes tested, apart from which pack's cycle count is shown when sysfs has a `BAT*` directory that UPower does not list. Three issues remain: packs that report `charge_*` values (which the PR description says are handled) can read above 100%, the multi-pack path drops the UPower charge thresholds, and devices DisplayDevice does not count are added to the totals.

| Surface Book 2 fixture (stubbed `upower`, synthetic sysfs) | Merge base | This PR | DisplayDevice formula |
|---|---|---|---|
| percentage | 80% | 71% | 71.25% |
| state | pending-charge | discharging | discharging |
| rate / size | 0W / 19Wh | 14.7W / 72Wh | 14.66 W / 72.81 Wh |
| time / cycles | blank / 86 | 3h 32m / 86, 129 | about 3.5 h |

**Verified:** the new test case fails on the merge base with the same output reported in #11990 (80%, pending-charge, 0W, 19Wh, blank time, cycles 86) and passes on this head. It runs through the existing `test/shell` glob.

### Percentage above 100% on multi-pack machines with `charge_*` packs

In the multi-pack path the numerator and denominator use different voltages:

```text
pack_energy = charge_now × voltage_now    (live voltage, bin/omarchy-battery-status:55-58)
pack_full   = UPower "energy-full:"       (charge_full × design voltage, line 46)
percentage  = Σ pack_energy / Σ pack_full (line 143)
```

UPower converts both current and full charge with the pack's design voltage (`up_device_battery_charge_to_energy` in `src/up-device-battery.c`, UPower 1.91.3 and 1.91.4). ACPI charge-unit packs expose only the nominal `voltage_min_design`, which UPower then uses, and a charged Li-ion pack's live voltage sits above that nominal value, so the ratio overshoots near full and undershoots near empty. By source reading (not run), the same mismatch occurs when a pack exposes `charge_full` and `energy_now` but no `energy_full`, because UPower then uses charge units while the script reads `energy_now`.

Synthetic two-pack cases (stubbed `upower`, typical Li-ion voltages, not measured hardware):

| Case | This PR | DisplayDevice formula | With suggested change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Both packs full on AC, `voltage_now` 13.05 V / 13.0 V, design 11.4 V | `114%` | 100% | 100% |
| Both packs at 95%, one charging at 13.1 V, the other idle at 13.0 V | `109%`, `-27m to full` | 95%, about 18m | 95%, `16m` |
| Both packs at 50%, one discharging | 51% | 50% | 50% |

**Impact:** on multi-battery machines whose packs report charge rather than energy, the power panel and the battery notification can show a percentage above 100% near full charge, and a negative time to full while charging near full. At mid charge the error is about one point. Energy-unit packs (including the Surface Book 2 and T480 fixtures above) and single-pack machines are unaffected, outside the cases in the last section.

**Suggested change:** take each pack's energy from UPower's `energy:` line, which has the same basis as `energy-full` and is what DisplayDevice sums, and keep sysfs only for the live rate:

```bash
pack_energy=$(awk '$1 == "energy:" { print $2; exit }' <<<"$info")
```

With that one line replacing lines 55-61, the cases above read as in the last column, and all 12 single-pack scenarios plus the energy-unit multi-pack scenarios (including this PR's own test numbers) produce byte-identical output. A `charge_*` two-pack case in `battery-status-test.sh` would cover this.

### Multi-pack path drops UPower charge thresholds

`battery_info` is only set in the single-pack branch, so on multi-pack machines lines 169-170 read an empty string and the thresholds come only from the first `BAT*/charge_control_*_threshold` file in sysfs.

| Case (synthetic) | Merge base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| T480 on AC, UPower thresholds 75/80, sysfs thresholds 0/100 | `threshold 75-80%` | `threshold 0-100%` |
| Two packs pending-charge on AC, UPower thresholds 75/80, no sysfs threshold files | `state holding`, `Holding at 75-80%` | `state pending-charge`, no threshold, `Battery 80%  ·   left` |

**Impact:** the panel's charge-limit value and the notification's "Holding at" wording change whenever the multi-pack path runs, and the PR description does not mention it. Which source is more accurate is a separate question (UPower's values can be the hwdb offer rather than the enforced limit), but single-pack and multi-pack machines now behave differently.

**Suggested change:** set `battery_info="$first_info"` in both branches to keep the previous source, or describe the change in the PR if it is intended.

### Devices UPower does not treat as system batteries are counted

`grep BAT` keeps any object path containing `BAT`, and the new loop adds every match. Two inputs reach it that DisplayDevice does not count (a pack UPower has already removed, and supplies with `power supply: no`):

- A pack that disappears between `upower -e` and `upower -i`. The real `upower` client (1.91.3, against a test D-Bus service) exits 0 and prints a dump with `native-path: (null)`, `power supply: no` and no `state:` line, so the `[[ -n $native ]]` check does not skip it. The race window is short.
- A device-scoped supply whose kernel name contains `BAT`. UPower lists it under a path containing that name (for example `battery_BAT0`) with `power supply: no`. None of the peripheral drivers checked uses such a name, and a generic HID battery can match only through its serial, so this is rare.

**Impact:** when a vanished pack is listed first and the remaining pack is fully charged, the output has an empty `state` line and UPower's thresholds are lost. When a device-scoped supply is listed after the laptop's pack, a single-battery laptop moves onto the multi-pack path, takes a discharging peripheral's state (`discharging` while charging on AC) and loses its thresholds.

**Suggested change:** skip those devices the same way DisplayDevice does, right after the native-path check:

```bash
[[ $(awk '$1 == "power" && $2 == "supply:" { print $3; exit }' <<<"$info") == "no" ]] && continue
```

In the same synthetic runs this line corrected both cases and left 26 of 27 earlier scenarios byte-identical, including the PR's test numbers. The one change was the vanished-pack scenario, which then reports `fully-charged`.

**Additional notes:**
- A sysfs attribute can pass `-r` and still fail on read (the ACPI driver returns ENODEV when a value is unknown). `$(<file)` then yields an empty string with status 0, awk turns it into 0, and the UPower fallback is never reached. In the multi-pack loop a failed `energy_now` or `voltage_now` read now moves the headline percentage (for example 67% to 40% in a synthetic two-pack case when the idle pack's `energy_now` read fails). Taking energy from UPower as suggested above removes the energy half; accepting a sysfs rate only when it is numeric would cover the rest.
- The kernel ABI defines `cycle_count` 0 as "not available", and UPower treats it as unknown. With one count per pack, a pack without data now reads as `cycles 0, 129`. Skipping zero values would avoid that.

**Related open PRs:** #10392 (DisplayDevice when more than one pack is listed) and #12445 (its own aggregation loop, which also says it closes #11990) change the same lines in `bin/omarchy-battery-status` and extend the same test. #12445 makes different choices (charging over discharging, time from the most urgent pack), so its dual-pack fixture expects `2h` where this branch's formula gives 5h (computed from the fixture values, not run). Maintainers will likely want to pick one approach.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head against the merge base, with UPower 1.91.3/1.91.4 and Linux 7.2 source read for the unit, state and threshold semantics. The changed test and differential scenarios (single-pack and multi-pack, both output modes) ran in an isolated sandbox with a stubbed `upower` and a synthetic power-supply directory. The vanished-pack and peripheral cases used the real `upower` client against a test D-Bus service. No real multi-battery hardware or running `upowerd` was used; DisplayDevice figures are computed from UPower's source or quoted from the linked issue and PR threads. The full `test/shell` suite was not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
